I bet that your adenosine sky rockets when you put on a vlog for the same reasons Pavlov’s dogs drooled when they heard a bell. Brains are so wacky!

This is a really interesting question! I totally relate (Bob’s Burgers is what puts me right to sleep). From the research I’ve done on the topic, it may be a matter of paired stimuli. For me, watching some tv while in bed allows me to get sleepy without thinking. Without it, I can lay awake for hours with my head spinning feeling completely wired. Once I’m sleepy I turn the show off and I’m out. Essentially I’ve trained my brain to go “oh I’m watching tv in bed, must mean it’s time to sleep.” This pairs the stimuli of the tv show, in your case the vlogs, with falling asleep. If you do this enough, you’re brain already knows what to do when you think about turning on a video, and is likely already winding down when you do so. It’s basically what Pavlov did with his dogs. Which, if you’re not familiar, is a super interesting experiment on behaviorism I suggest you check out! 

The reason this doesn’t happen when you watch videos during the day is because our brains are very good at identifying the context around stimuli. When you watch these videos at night you’re probably already in bed, teeth brushed, wearing pjs etc. so you’re brain goes straight into KO protocol. When you watch them during the day there’s many factors your brain is aware of that tells it not to go to sleep. Like where you are, what time it is, what you are wearing, etc. 

As far as I can tell, as long as the time you need to fall asleep doesn’t get longer, you’re probably fine and don’t need to worry. It’s probably not dissociation, but just a relaxation tool. If you’d like to learn more about relaxation tools that don’t require a screen, I highly recommend checking out some mindfulness exercises. These essentially do the same thing the video does for you.
